finding.claim: The /settings/email endpoint uses @login_optional instead of @login_required, so unauthenticated users can reach the email-change operation. g.uid is None for anonymous requests, and set_email is called with uid=None. Depending on the real set_email implementation, this could update a null/guest account, raise errors, or enable account takeover via email change. The sibling /settings/password route correctly uses @login_required, which shows the intent.
finding.source: Unauthenticated HTTP POST to /settings/email with no session cookie
finding.sink: set_email(g.uid, ...) at routes.py:37, a state-changing account email modification

trace.note: login_optional sets g.uid = session.get('uid'), which is None when no session exists, and never aborts
Route /settings/email registered with methods=POST and decorated with @login_optional
set_email(g.uid, ...) called with a possibly None uid, with no authentication check

finding.guards_checked: login_required is not applied to this route. There is no inline check of g.uid. No CSRF protection is visible in the file, and the session is a Flask cookie session. set_email is a stub (line 48), so downstream validation could not be confirmed. The /settings/password route uses login_required, so it is not affected.

verdict.reason: routes.py:35 applies @login_optional, which at routes.py:22 sets g.uid = session.get("uid") and never aborts, so an anonymous POST reaches set_email(g.uid, ...) at routes.py:37 with uid=None and no inline check. The sibling route at routes.py:42 uses @login_required, which aborts with 401 at routes.py:12, so this route is missing the guard it should have. set_email is a stub (routes.py:48-49), so the actual impact depends on its real implementation.

verdict_facts.reason: routes.py:35 applies @login_optional, which at routes.py:22 sets g.uid = session.get("uid") without aborting, so an anonymous POST reaches set_email(g.uid=None, ...) at routes.py:37 with no check, whereas the sibling route at routes.py:42 uses @login_required; set_email (routes.py:48) is a stub, so the impact depends on the real implementation, but the missing authentication guard is real.
